title.en: Complete elliptic integrals K(m), E(m) approximation

summary: Evaluate the polynomial-logarithmic approximations to complete K(m) and E(m) on arrays with 0<=m<=1.

capability: Complete elliptic integrals K(m) and E(m) approximation
Evaluate polynomial-logarithmic approximations to complete K(m) and E(m) on arrays with 0<=m<=1.
operation: piecewise numerical approximation in the elliptic parameter m
modulus squared -> K and E arrays
discovery.model: Piecewise numerical approximation in the elliptic parameter m.
discovery.geometry: Elementwise over any NumPy-compatible numeric shape.
discovery.boundary: Only finite m in [0,1] is accepted; m=1 uses the mathematical endpoint limits.

identity.direction: modulus squared to K and E arrays
identity.definition: Evaluate the fixed polynomial-logarithmic approximation elementwise and assign K(1)=+Inf, E(1)=1.
identity.model: Piecewise numerical approximation in the elliptic parameter m.
identity.geometry: Elementwise over any NumPy-compatible numeric shape.
identity.coordinates: m dimensionless; K and E dimensionless.
identity.boundary: Only finite m in [0,1] is accepted; m=1 uses the mathematical endpoint limits.
assumptions: Input is real and finite after float conversion.
The approximation is not a general symbolic elliptic-integral solver.

outputs.name: complete_k
outputs.description: First-kind complete elliptic integral K(m), polynomial-log approximation.
outputs.constraints: Finite approximation for m<1; +Inf at every m=1 element, representing the divergent integral.

outputs.name: complete_e
outputs.description: Second-kind complete elliptic integral E(m), polynomial-log approximation.
outputs.constraints: Finite approximation for m<1; exactly 1 at every m=1 element.

preconditions: Input is real and finite after float conversion.
supported: Interior values, mixed arrays, and endpoint limits covered by direct tests.
excluded: m outside [0,1], complex values, and an error guarantee outside the tested approximation domain.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: ValueError is raised when any entry is nonfinite or outside [0,1].
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: NumPy arithmetic failures propagate if an accepted calculation is not representable.
failure_semantics.nonconvergence: Not applicable; the approximation is direct and elementwise.
failure_semantics.partial_results: No tuple is returned for an invalid array.

example.description: Evaluate interior and endpoint values in separate and mixed arrays.
example.code:
import numpy as np
from scirel.field import evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals
k, e = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([0.5, 0.9]))
assert np.all(np.isfinite(k)) and np.all(np.isfinite(e))
k1, e1 = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([1.0]))
assert np.isposinf(k1[0]) and e1[0] == 1.0
km, em = evaluate_complete_elliptic_integrals(np.array([0.5, 1.0]))
assert np.isposinf(km[1]) and em[1] == 1.0
example.expected: Interior K and E values are finite; every m=1 entry returns K=+Inf and E=1.

scope: Source polynomial-log evaluation against an independent recomputation.
Elementwise analytic endpoint limits and unchanged invalid-input rejection.

Independent evidence (tests/field/test_complete_elliptic_integrals_approx_evidence.py): K and E are compared with mpmath at 50 decimal digits against the tabulated absolute bound of 2e-8 published in Abramowitz and Stegun 17.3.34/17.3.36 rather than against a bound measured here, on a grid that reaches m = 1 - 1e-10; the endpoint limits are assigned elementwise; and the coefficient of ln(1/p) near m = 1 is localised to 1/2 by differencing two small-p values.
verification.evidence_ceiling: The direct tests in tests/field/test_filament_coil_green.py separately check fixed-polynomial evaluation, elementwise endpoint/invalid-input behavior, and a predetermined interior/near-one grid against independent scipy.special.ellipk/ellipe. The accuracy budget is the 2e-8 absolute approximation error printed for the matching coefficients in Abramowitz and Stegun 17.3.34/17.3.36, plus 128 binary64 eps times the reference magnitude for evaluation roundoff. tests/cross_domain/test_legacy_admission_regressions.py supplies an additional endpoint assertion. Shared-file Green-field tests are not elliptic-approximation evidence. Sampled success is not a new continuous-domain binary64 error proof or physical field validation. C1 evidence replaces SciPy with a 50-digit second source and applies the published 2e-8 absolute bound as a declared threshold. The bound is verified on the sampled grid only, so no continuous error bound is proven; and nothing here establishes that this standalone approximation is suitable inside a field evaluation, which the Green kernel does not use it for.
known_limitations: The independent SciPy comparison is limited to the predetermined test grid; it is numerical approximation evidence, not experimental or finite-wire validation.

The fixed coefficients have a published real-arithmetic absolute approximation bound of 2e-8 for 0<=m<1, not a universal relative 1e-8 binary64 guarantee. Use scipy.special.ellipk and ellipe when higher accuracy is needed.
The endpoint value is the analytic limit rather than a guarded surrogate; K(1) must not be treated as a finite magnetic field.
The approximation is evaluated only on real `m` in `[0,1]`; no analytic continuation or complex-modulus path is provided.

The 2e-8 figure is verified as an observed maximum on the sampled grid; the interval between sampled m values is not covered by proof, and the published claim remains a tabulated real-arithmetic bound rather than a binary64 guarantee.
The logarithmic-coefficient check localises the coefficient to 0.5 within 1e-2; it distinguishes 1/2 from the other plausible coefficients and does not measure the tabulated digits.

basis.statement: SciPy is replaced by a 50-digit second source and the published 2e-8 absolute bound is applied as a declared threshold. The bound is verified on the sampled grid only, so no continuous error bound is proven, and nothing here establishes suitability inside a field evaluation.
